issues.detail: The Greek 'μη παρεστιν' (not having/possessing) is rendered as 'không có', but the context of the sentence is a conditional result. The Vietnamese phrasing 'Vì ai không có những điều này thì bị mù' suggests a causal 'Because anyone who doesn't have...', whereas the Greek 'ω γαρ μη παρεστιν' functions more as a conditional 'For he who does not have...'. More importantly, 'τυφλος εστιν μυωπαζων' describes someone who is both blind and short-sighted; the Vietnamese 'bị mù, không thấy xa' captures this well, but the omission of the specific nuance of 'μυωπαζων' (short-sighted/near-sighted) as a distinct physical state compared to just 'not seeing far' is minor. The primary issue is the slight shift in the logical flow of the conditional.
